A foresight address by the Comptroller General is GAO-06-1041CG, delivered July 28, 2006. He spoke to the World Future Society Conference in Toronto, Canada. The talk surveys the megatrends and long-term challenges facing the United States. It explains GAO's role in government oversight. And it presses the need for foresight and strategic planning in how government runs.

The presentation sets current choices against long horizons. Fiscal strain, demographic shift, and global change run through it. GAO's own shift toward long-term simulation and forward watch is part of the story. Readers get the watchdog chief's public case for planning ahead in one text. It is a speech record, not an audit, and it frames the themes that drive much of GAO's 2006 work.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-990cg:
Citizen duty in a time of debt and drift is the theme of a speech, GAO-06-990CG, given on July 11, 2006. The Comptroller General spoke in Dallas to the Sons of the American Revolution, in the 100th year since that group got its charter from Congress. He spoke as office holder, citizen, father, and member.

He asked what the nation's founders would say if they came back now. They would cheer a republic past 200 years, he argued, and its spread of civil rights. They would worry over career politics and lost thrift, in leaders and in homes. The speech calls for modern-day patriots to serve, not just hold office.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-353cg: This 2007 GAO report takes a hard look at saving Our Future Requires Tough Choices Today. Congress relies on GAO for straight fact-finding on federal programs. Findings like these push agencies to fix the problems GAO reports. The library keeps it as part of the public record.
podcast-joerogan-vNkXIKijzcg:
Attorney Aaron Siri makes his legal case on vaccines in episode 2462 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Siri represents clients who say they were injured by vaccines and has sued for records from health agencies. He is a leading lawyer for the informed consent movement.

Siri walks through the liability shield that protects vaccine makers and the system that pays injury claims. He shares what agency documents showed when his firm forced their release. Rogan asks about mandates and what parents are told before shots. The episode gives the legal critique of vaccine policy its fullest hearing on the show.
